name: 둥근 지붕 갈빗대(동쪽 벽, 가운데로 휨, 1×3) (dome rib east)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/dome rib east

surfaces.part: rib shaft (vertical wooden beam with gold bands)
brick wall segment with ledge at top

answer.evidence: The main body is a narrow vertical rib, 6 px wide in rows 19-42, with gold bands at rows 17-18 and 30-31. It is drawn as a flat vertical face with a lit left edge and a dark right edge. No band ends in a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and there is no ellipse, roof or visible contents. The gray stone foot at rows 43-47 is a small tapered, stepped plate of 4 rows with no separate top surface. The brick wall above it is also a flat face. Because the object is mounted flat on a wall, it is read as a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall vertical wooden rib with banded joints and a lighter highlight stripe. It shows about 4 brown steps plus darker band and shadow tones, and the grain is varied with no flat areas. The measured facts support this: 13 visible tones per tile is above the hedge (9) and below the well (20) and stall (17), and near-flat coverage is 0%. Dark edge pixels are 40% near-neutral, close to the Beodeul bench (44%) and well (33%), so the outline is mixed, not a uniform black sticker line. It is a thin prop that is a little simpler than the roofed well and the stall, but a careful artist would accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: rib shaft (wooden beam with two gold bands) over the wall backdrop
stone foot/bracket at the bottom, tapering

answer.evidence: The main body is a narrow vertical wooden rib (6 px wide, rows 0-42) with two 2-row gold bands. It is drawn as a flat face with a dark right-hand edge and no horizontal surface. The bottom foot (rows 43-47) widens to 10 px and then tapers to 4 px. Its light top rows 43-44 are only a 1-2 row rim or lip with no ellipse and no eave shadow. The 16 px wide rows 0-15 are the wall backdrop (stone bricks over a checker pattern), not a part with a top. There is no isometric side face. This is a flat, front-facing wall-mounted element.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall wood-and-stone rib column. It has about 5 lightness steps on the wood: highlight edge, light plank, mid, dark and deep shadow, plus a banded section. It shows 13 visible tones per full tile, which sits between prop-hedge (9) and prop-well-roofed (20) and well above the thin props. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the grain and band variation are visible. Only 40% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is partly tinted and partly dark neutral, which I call mixed. It is not a uniform black sticker line. The candidate has fewer total colours (24) than the richer references (38-40) and slightly less surface grain than the well or the stall. That is acceptable for a plain structural rib, and a careful artist could place it next to the references without it looking flat.

surfaces.part: wooden rib shaft with two gold bands
background stone wall bricks and ledge strip beside the rib
stone corbel foot at the bottom

answer.evidence: The main body is a narrow vertical wooden rib, 6 px wide, running rows 0-42. Two gold bands cross it at rows 17-18 and 30-31. It is drawn face-on as a vertical strip with no horizontal surface, no ellipse, and no roof or awning plane. The widening at rows 43-44 (width 10, light band) tapering to width 4 by row 47 reads as a 2-row rim over a front-facing corbel, not a top surface. The light line at row 11 with dark rows 12-15 beside the rib is part of the background wall ledge, not the rib. For a flat wall-mounted piece this is a plain front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin 1x3 vertical rib: a wooden beam with banding and a stone or bracket section. It shows about 5 lightness steps across the wood (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) and grain variation along the beam. Measured facts: 13 visible tones per tile, which is above prop-hedge (9) and a little below prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 40% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, similar to the bench (44%) and well (33%). The outline is therefore mixed: partly brown-tinted and partly near-black, not a uniform black sticker line. Texture is moderate rather than rich, and density is a bit lighter than the best references. For a narrow structural prop, an artist would accept it next to the references without it looking flat or sticker-like.

surfaces.part: vertical rib shaft (wooden beam with gold bands)
stone base/foot at bottom of rib

answer.evidence: The object is a long, narrow vertical wooden rib (6-8 px wide, rows 0-47) with gold bands at rows 17-18 and 30-31, flat-mounted on an east wall. The shading is a flat vertical gradient (left lighter, right darker) with no horizontal surface, no ellipse and no front-edge line with eave shadow at the top. The stone foot at rows 43-47 is a small bracket that steps in (width 10, 8, 6, 4) and reads as a base/corbel rather than a top surface. It is a flat wall-mounted piece seen face-on, so it reads as front elevation, which is acceptable for wall_mounted.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical wooden rib with banded joins and a stone-like block. It shows about 5 lightness steps on the wood: highlight, light, mid, dark and a deep edge. Grain and highlight dots break up the surface, so no large area is flat. It measures 13 visible tones per tile, above prop-hedge (9) and in range of the bench, stall and well references (up to 20), and near-flat coverage is 0%. Its dark edge pixels are 40% neutral, close to the bench (44%) and well (33%) references, so I read the outline as mixed: partly tinted dark brown, partly near-black. It is somewhat simpler than the roofed well or the cheese stall, which carry more clusters and tile-by-tile detail, so density is slightly lower. That is acceptable for a plain structural piece, and the piece does not look like a flat sticker beside the references.
